articles.author: Abdullah Alhumsi
articles.description:
Every Laravel app breaks in production. The question is: do you 
I got tired of checking logs manually and built a package that 
Here's how I built it and what I learned.
Most Laravel error monitoring solutions are either too expensive,
I wanted something that:
Sends alerts instantly to channels I already use
Shows me exactly what broke and where
Suggests what to do about it
Is dead simple to install
So I built laravel-error-notifier.
The package hooks into Laravel's exception handler and sends 
A Telegram alert looks like this:
🚨 EMERGENCY | your-app.com
QueryException
app/Services/UserService.php:45
Suggestion: Check your migration status
composer require alhumsi/laravel-error-notifier
php artisan vendor:publish --tag=error-notifier-config

Add your channel credentials to .env:
ERROR_NOTIFIER_TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN=your-token
https://hooks.slack.com/...
https://discord.com/api/webhooks/...
That's it. No manual registration needed — the package 
The package uses three core abstractions:
AnalyzerInterface — maps exception types to severity levels.
QueryException is critical. A ValidationException is error.
MessageFormatterInterface — formats the alert for each channel.
NotifierInterface — sends the formatted message via HTTP.
In config/error-notifier.php:
'levels' => [
    'emergency' => ['slack', 'telegram'],
    'critical'  => ['slack'],
    'error'     => ['discord'],
],

High-severity alerts go to Slack where your team sees them 
'icons' => [
    'emergency' => '🚨',
    'critical'  => '🔥',
    'error'     => '❌',
    'warning'   => '⚠️',
],

Small detail but it makes alerts scannable at a glance.
1. Contracts make packages extensible.
2. Auto-discovery matters.
3. Write tests from day one.
composer require alhumsi/laravel-error-notifier

GitHub: https://github.com/Alhumsiabdo/laravel-error-notifier
https://packagist.org/packages/alhumsi/laravel-error-notifier
If you find it useful, a ⭐ on GitHub goes a long way.
What error monitoring are you using in your Laravel apps? 
I'd love to know in the comments.
articles.title: How I Built a Laravel Package to Send Error Alerts to Telegram, Slack & Discord

Next.js is not a typical React app. With the App Router, your code runs in multiple environments — the server, the edge, and the browser — sometimes in the same request. This makes feature flags both more powerful and more complex than in a single-page application.

Server-Side Rendering creates a decision point. When a Server Component renders on the server, you need the flag value before sending HTML to the client. If you evaluate flags only on the client, users see a flash of the wrong content (or a loading spinner) before the correct variant appears.
Edge Middleware runs before rendering. Next.js middleware can redirect or rewrite requests at the edge, befor…

articles.author: Osmium
articles.description:
Why Bother


I have a two-node Proxmox VE cluster, and two-node clusters have an inherent distributed systems problem: if either machine goes down, the surviving node can't tell whether it should keep running or not. Running a quorum usually requires a majority vote, which normally means at least three voters. With only two machines, one vote each, lose one and you're down to one vote. No quorum and your cluster stops.
The solution is a quorum device. Proxmox supports corosync-qnetd, a lightweight daemon from the corosync project that acts as a third-party tiebreaker. A qnetd doesn't participate in storage or compute, it just casts the deciding vote during a split-brain scenario. By bringing the total vote count to three, the cluster maintains a majority requirement and consequently, if an…
